name: Z Tether Studio
description:
I am building an android app (attached) for tethering Nikon Z.

What I want is:
A photo editing tool first, with advanced tools like denoise, crop etc.
Tether and control Nikon Z cameras, with remote control
Ability to create project & stage clients so images are assigned to subjects
Publish images, either to My Firebase photoshoot (me only), or (public users) to their Google Drive, Social Media, Local Storage, SFTP of their choosing.

Extra features would be cool, like adding GPS location to EXIF data and so on.
I want it to work on tablet and mobile. So finger-friendly editing with pinch-pull to zoom in/out and gesture control.

I have built some so far, but want to re-align so it is something i can publish to the public as a cheaper basic editing tool. I don't want AI inside the tool, other than perhaps TFLite models that denoise / background blur. Masking / removing / clone tools would be cool.

So far: 

This application is a professional, high-performance Tethered Photoshoot Console & Digital Asset Management System designed for high-volume event photographers (such as portrait, commercial, or on-stage event studios). It is built specifically to bridge physical professional cameras with a tablet-focused mobile workflow, combining real-time camera telemetry, live raw asset processing, local database management, and cloud-powered AI enhancements.
Here is a comprehensive breakdown of what the application does, structured by its core modules:
1. Hardware Tethering & Camera Control (PTP over USB-C)
At the heart of the system is a physical USB-C tethering subsystem that talks to cameras directly using standard Picture Transfer Protocol (PTP):
Dynamic Connection Lifecycle: Monitors the USB bus for compatible camera connections. When a device is connected, the app requests dynamic hardware permissions in Android and opens a high-speed UsbDeviceConnection.
MTP Real-Time Event Poller: Runs a high-priority background polling loop listening to the USB Interrupt endpoint. The moment a photographer presses the physical camera's shutter button, the app instantly catches the ObjectAdded (shutter release) event.
Automated Asset Ingestion: Once a new photo event is received, the app immediately pulls the raw file bytes directly from the camera’s buffer into the tablet’s cache memory.
2. High-Fidelity Asset Pipeline (RAW Decoder & Cropper)
Because professional cameras output complex RAW files, the app features a sophisticated client-side rendering pipeline:
RAW & NEF Processing: Extracts high-fidelity, color-accurate embedded JPEGs and previews from RAW camera formats (such as Nikon's .nef or generic .raw) using Android's native software decoders and EXIF parsing.
Interactive Bounding Viewport: Features a high-precision, tablet-optimized visual Cropper. It displays modern bracketed crop corners that support multi-touch dragging (using a generous grab radius for accurate tablet stylus/finger control) as well as full center-bounding-box translations.
Live Presets & Filter Matrix: Applies GPU-accelerated adjustments (Brightness, Saturation, Contrast, Vignette, Blur, and custom color overlays) in real time using Jetpack Compose color matrix graphics filters.
3. Cloud-Offloaded AI Image Restoration (Denoising Proxy)
For low-light scenarios or high-ISO noise, the application integrates an automated AI Denoise workflow:
Proxy Optimization: Since RAW files are too heavy for cellular bandwidth, the app dynamically generates a downscaled high-contrast image proxy, optimizing bandwidth and memory usage to prevent tablet OutOfMemory crashes.
Firebase Cloud Functions Bridge: Securely POSTs base64 image data to a cloud-offloaded microservice.
NAFNet AI Model Integration: The cloud backend connects with the Replicate API to run the NAFNet Image Denoising model, restoring clarity and sharpening details. The result is returned to the tablet as a cloud-hosted preview and immediately overlaid onto the viewport.
4. Client Onboarding & Session Mapping
The app links individual photos to specific clients or subjects to streamline post-event delivery:
Local Database Persistence (Room): Uses a secure, local Room SQLite database to store shoot configurations, photographer brand preferences, onboarded clients, and dynamic photo assignments.
Live Firebase Sync: Automatically fetches and synchronizes event details, visual theme brandings, and registration lists in real-time from a cloud Firestore database.
On-Stage Handshake: Allows photographers to manually onboard clients on-the-fly, select active models for upcoming captures, and seamlessly upload selected portraits to a remote sharing portal.
Offline Standalone Mode: Provides a prominent bypass menu, allowing photographers to configure a local photoshoot and run high-speed tethering in completely offline environments without any remote Firestore or network requirements.
Key Technical Stack & Architectural Highlights
UI & Theming: Built entirely on Jetpack Compose with a premium Material Design 3 (M3) custom dark theme featuring high-contrast accents, custom status indicators, split-pane layouts, and a dedicated tether console dashboard.
State Management: Adheres to modern MVVM standards utilizing ViewModel, unidirectional state flow (StateFlow/MutableStateFlow), and Coroutines for non-blocking file and USB-C transactions.
Robust Concurrency: Leverages asynchronous Kotlin Coroutines to isolate intensive disk I/O, heavy image rendering, and USB connection management away from the main UI thread.

Make v1 a local-first photo editor + optional Nikon tether add-on, not a cloud/AI/photoshoot console first.

Big findings:

Urgent: app/src/main/assets/service_account.json contains a Firebase service-account private key. Remove it, rotate/revoke it immediately, and never ship service accounts inside Android apps.
The app is currently too event-studio/Firebase-specific for a public low-cost editor.
Nikon tethering exists, but PTP support is still basic/risky: hardcoded vendor checks, limited object size cap, no robust Nikon capability discovery, no USB device filter in manifest.
Editing is currently bitmap/JPEG-preview based, not true RAW development.
Publishing only really supports your Firebase workflow; Drive/SFTP/social/local export are not yet separate destinations.

Recommended product shape:

Free/basic public app

Import JPEG/RAW preview
Crop, straighten, exposure, contrast, saturation, white balance, sharpen, vignette
Finger-friendly zoom/pan/crop
Local export/share sheet
Project/session albums
No login required

Paid/pro tier

Nikon Z USB tethering
Assign shots to clients/subjects
Batch export
SFTP / Drive publishing
TFLite denoise/background blur
EXIF GPS injection

Technical refactor:

Split into modules: editor, library, tether-nikon, publishing, photoshoot.
Replace cloud AI denoise with optional on-device TFLite later.
Use Android Storage Access Framework for user-chosen local/Drive-style destinations; Android’s SAF is designed for browsing/opening documents across providers.
For Google Drive, use Drive API upload flows rather than Firebase proxy publishing.
Keep Nikon tethering, but treat it as a compatibility-tested premium feature. Nikon’s 2026 Remote Module SDK supports many Z-series bodies, but it appears desktop-focused, so Android PTP may still need custom testing.

Best MVP name/positioning:
“Tether Studio Lite — mobile photo editor with optional Nikon Z tethering.”

Your next code priority should be: remove secrets, strip Firebase from the default app path, and make local editing/export excellent first
